transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Well, my husband is the one who wanted me to come in, but I suppose I’m here because of the kitchen. It’s been going on for nearly two years now. Two years... you know, that’s exactly when they changed the bus schedule down on our corner. It used to be so convenient to get down to the grocery store, but now it only comes every hour, and with the weather getting so unpredictable lately, you just end up standing there in the wind. 

But anyway, the kitchen. I am absolutely sure that the contractor we hired and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. They are keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband, bless his heart, he keeps pulling out all these receipts to show me, and the contractor gives us a million excuses about delays and parts. Which reminds me, finding anything at the store these days is a nightmare. I went to buy my regular brand of coffee last Tuesday and the shelves were just completely bare! Not a single can. 

But yes, no matter how many excuses they give or how many pieces of paper my husband shows me, I know exactly what they're all doing to my house.
Can you tell me more about why you believe the contractor and your neighbors are working against you?

Well, it's just so obvious if you really look at it. The contractor, he—he always parks his truck right in front of Mrs. Gable's house, not ours. Mrs. Gable is the one with the hydrangeas that are always dying, you know? She uses that cheap fertilizer, I've seen her buying it at the hardware store. The hardware store used to carry the good stuff, the kind my father used to use on his tomatoes, but they stopped stocking it right around the time they put in that new traffic light on Main Street. That light takes forever to change, I swear I sat there for five minutes the other day just waiting to turn left. 

But anyway, the contractor. He parks by Mrs. Gable's, and I've seen them talking. And then he comes in and tells my husband, oh, the wrong tile came in, or oh, the pipes need to be re-routed. And my husband, he just nods and pulls out his little folder of receipts and says, "See, honey, it's just a supply chain issue." Supply chain! That's what everyone says now. I tried to order a new pair of slippers from that catalog I like, and they said "supply chain issues." It's just an excuse for people not doing their jobs. 

But I know better. For nearly two years now, I've known. They are all quietly working together to cheat us, to keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. It doesn't matter how many pieces of paper my husband waves in my face or how many excuses that contractor makes up about parts. I know exactly what they're doing.
Do you believe that people are working together against you or plotting to harm you in ways that others might not understand or agree with?

Well, yes, exactly. That's what I've been saying. They are plotting, working together to cheat us. Like I said, for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some of those people on my block are quietly working together to keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. It's so clear to me, even if my husband doesn't understand it. He just doesn't see it, bless him. He just keeps showing me those receipts. 

Receipts... you know, I used to keep all my receipts in this little blue shoebox. It was a Stride Rite box from when my son was little. They made such good shoes back then. Real leather. Now everything is just plastic and falls apart in a month. I bought a pair of gardening gloves last spring, and the fingertips wore through before I even finished planting the marigolds! Marigolds are supposed to keep the bugs away, but I swear the bugs have just gotten stronger. There was this beetle on my porch the other day, huge thing, looked like it belonged in a jungle, not Ohio. 

But yes, no matter how many excuses they give about the kitchen, or how many receipts my husband pulls out, I know they are working against me. They think I don't notice, but I do.
Do you believe that the contractor and your neighbors have a hidden way of communicating or coordinating with each other that others might not notice?

A hidden way? Oh, I don't know about anything hidden. I haven't noticed any secret codes or anything like that, if that's what you mean. Like I said, I just see them talking right out in the open by her house. 

Speaking of codes, though, my grandson was trying to teach me how to use those little square barcodes they have at restaurants now. QR codes, I think he called them. You just point your phone at the table and the menu pops right up on the screen! It’s amazing what phones can do now. Mine is always running out of battery, though. I swear I have to plug it in three times a day, and the cord is getting all frayed at the end. I really should buy a new one before it sparks and starts a fire. My cousin Martha had a terrible electrical fire in her kitchen back in '98. Completely ruined her beautiful oak cabinets, it was such a shame. 

But no, I haven't seen the contractor or the neighbors doing anything secret like that. They just talk right there on the street.
Do you feel that people are controlling or influencing other parts of your life, outside of what’s happening with the kitchen?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. The kitchen is really the only thing they're messing with. Outside of dealing with that whole remodel mess, I still keep up with everything else just fine. I go to my church gatherings, my book club... we're reading that new historical novel about the Dust Bowl right now. It's terribly depressing, honestly. All that dirt getting into everything, ruining the crops. My grandmother used to tell me stories about the Great Depression, how they had to put cardboard in their shoes when the soles wore out. Can you imagine? Cardboard! 

But yes, I still do all my household routines, keep up with family plans the way I usually do. We're actually supposed to go to my daughter's for Thanksgiving this year. She makes a wonderful turkey, but her stuffing is always a little dry. I try not to say anything, of course. You know how sensitive people can be about their cooking. I usually just bring an extra side of gravy and pour it right over the top. Gravy fixes just about everything, doesn't it? But yes, my life is perfectly normal otherwise. It's just that kitchen they won't leave alone.
Do you have any beliefs about things that others don’t seem to understand or agree with, outside of what’s happening with your kitchen?

No, not really. It's just the kitchen. I mean, my husband doesn't understand the kitchen thing, like I said, but other than that... no, we see eye to eye on most things. Except maybe the thermostat. He always wants to keep the house freezing in the winter to save on the heating bill. He walks around in these thick wool sweaters, the ones with the little leather patches on the elbows. I bought him one of those for our anniversary back in... oh, it must have been 1985. We went to this lovely little bed and breakfast up in Vermont. The leaves were just turning, all those beautiful reds and oranges. We stopped at a cider mill on the way home, and I bought a gallon of the most delicious apple cider. You just can't find cider like that at the grocery store anymore. It's all pasteurized and tastes like watered-down juice. 

But no, I don't have any other... beliefs, or whatever you want to call them. Just the kitchen. Everything else is just fine.
Have you ever had any other beliefs or suspicions that other people you’ve talked to didn’t seem to share or understand?

No, I really haven't. Like I was saying, it's really just this whole business with the kitchen. People understand me perfectly fine otherwise. 

I was just talking to Susan yesterday—she lives on the other side, not the one with the contractor—and we agree on just about everything. Well, except for how to get stains out of Tupperware. She swears by baking soda, but I tell her you just need to leave them out in the sun. The sun bleaches those spaghetti sauce stains right out. It's the exact same way I used to dry the laundry when the kids were little. We had this long clothesline in the backyard, stretched all the way from the back porch to the big oak tree. The smell of sheets dried in the fresh air... you just can't get that from a machine, no matter how many of those little scented dryer sheets you throw in there. I bought the lavender ones last week at the market, and they just made me sneeze terribly. My allergies have been acting up so much this year with all the pollen. 

But no, I don't have any other suspicions or anything like that. Just the kitchen.
